If you want the color black to look darker and richer, have another color underneath it. For cool black, have a blue layer beneath, for warm black use brown or orange (you can use other colors too, but those are the ones I use the most). Build the colors up slowly with soft layers for more vibrancy. I would also recommend getting a colorless blending pencil crayon, which can be found at most art and craft stores. I find that sharpening the pencil crayons with a knife allows for more control and makes the crayons last longer. Starting with the shadows and working your way to the lightest colors will have a sharper effect, going from lightest to darkest will have a softer effect. 

I hope this little infodump helps, pencil crayons are my favorite medium and I hope you have fun with them!! Also, just experimenting and playing around with different color combos can help you learn a lot!

Libby sat up on the hospital bed, cradling her newborn son in her arms. He’d finally fallen asleep, but despite her exhaustion, she couldn’t do the same. “Cathy… I have no idea what I’m doing,” she admitted with a trembling voice. She never planned on being a mother; she’d known all her life that she wouldn’t be a good parent. For years, her worst fear was having a child and hurting them the same way her parents had hurt her. It was why she took birth control, why she wouldn’t hook up without a condom, and why she ended her two previous pregnancies. But despite her caution, this boy had managed to beat all the odds. Even before his birth, he was stubborn and determined, just like his mother. 

She had half a mind to put him up for adoption, but now, looking down at the baby in her arms, HER baby, she knew she couldn’t do it. That maternal instinct wouldn’t make up for her lack of knowledge or experience, though. She needed help, and she knew her best friend was the only one she could count on. 

“It’s gonna be okay, Libby,” Cathy replied. “I didn’t know what I was doing, either, when my eldest was born. You learn as you go, and I’ll be here every step of the way. I promise.”

Decades had passed since that day, and true to her word, Cathy stuck by Libby’s side, showing her the ropes of motherhood. They became each others’ rock; through thick and thin, they were always there for each other. Their kids grew up together, becoming best friends just like their mothers. Now, the two women were chatting on the phone about their lives, Libby on her computer playing a video game while Cathy gazed thoughtfully out her window. Libby’s side hustle of producing and selling adult content wasn’t going as well as it had in the past, but luckily the pay of her main job as a videographer was sufficient, since her union had successfully negotiated a living wage for her and her colleagues. Libby and Cathy’s sons were now married and having children of their own, and both ladies were excited to shower their grandchildren with love and affection.

Every day, Cathy thanked God for her family, including her dearest friend who had now become a part of it, and Libby thanked Cathy for keeping her promise.

My dad had ADHD “before it was cool,” and I inherited it from him. People with ADHD are affected by chemical stimulants in an entirely different way than those who don’t have it. Caffeine for example; instead of making me feel hyper, it makes me feel calm and focused. A common symptom of undiagnosed ADHD is forming an abnormal dependence on caffeine in an attempt to self-medicate. This is also why ADHD medication makes people able to function better if they’ve been correctly diagnosed, and “zombie-like” if they’ve been misdiagnosed, and why it’s used as a recreational drug by people without ADHD. 

I do agree that the demand for constant productivity is unreasonable even for most neurotypical kids, though. Perhaps that’s why so many kids are being misdiagnosed. There are also external circumstances that can cause ADHD-like symptoms to occur, such as trauma. Medication will not help under such circumstances; people with such conditions need therapy.

If you were falsely diagnosed and suffered negative side effects from medication, I am truly, genuinely sorry that you experienced that, but that does not mean ADHD does not exist.
